Package hadur.bench

Class TeamReport

java.lang.Object
hadur.bench.TeamReport
public final class TeamReport extends Object
A5's team report: per opponent team, the score share and rounds won (as the TeamRumble scores them), how often a member of ours lived to the round's end, and the team gate's counts: faults and skipped turns, link reports rejected (LINK-3), shots that left with a living teammate truly in the lane (WEAVE-4), each member's count of enemies alive below the truth (WORLD-8), the members' own team records (T), and the data files the battle left behind (SHELF-2: no duel or melee shelf, and only the leader writes).

    render(String label, String robot, Map<Opponent,List<TeamReport.Battle>> results, int rounds, int width, int height, String host)
    As above; host (the CPU constant, the host description and the parallel width, as the duel report prints them) is a paragraph of its own under the title, followed by the skipped-turns tally and, when the members' R records carried it, the duress tally (issue #102, BENCH-12).
    (package private) static String
    renderOpponent(Opponent o, String label, List<TeamReport.Battle> candidate, List<TeamReport.Battle> baseline, String robot, String baselineRobot, int rounds, int width, int height, String host)
    One opposing team's own report for the per-opponent bench strategy (issue #102): the seed-by-seed table (with the baseline's share and the paired difference when a baseline ran), then the members' team records (T) for the diagnostics: the engine's count of bullets that hit our own members, drives the teammate fence replaced, and each member's own counts.
    (package private) static String
    renderPaired(Map<Opponent,List<TeamReport.Battle>> candidate, Map<Opponent,List<TeamReport.Battle>> baseline, String robot, String baselineRobot)
    The paired A/B table, per opponent team (issue #102, BENCH-2's convention): the candidate's and the baseline's battle against the same team at the same seed, so noise common to both cancels.
